reviewer.independence: The reviewer did not implement or edit the change, tests, admission gate or validation receipts. It inspected the working tree and diff read-only against the pinned base digests and produced only this review record. Source digests it could not hash itself were verified by the integrating agent with shasum and are re-derived fail-closed by validateXcbIntegrationAdmission.

sourceState.identity: Source digests identify the reviewed bytes; commits alone do not.

scope: The smart-mode explicit-ask fix: a bare shared link scored respond=true at 0.95 confidence in production (run bb48d8c4, docs.google.com share with no question), sending an unwanted reply. The four decision-language surfaces are tightened so only an explicit question, task request, or direct address can clear the 0.85 reply gate: the respond-phase instruction (habitat-program.ts), the rules contract embedded in the model context (habitat-agent.ts), the non-habitat CLASSIFIER_INSTRUCTIONS (decision.ts), and the DEFAULT_HABITAT_PLAN.guidance seed (contact-habitat.ts), plus regression pins in habitat-program.test.ts, habitat-agent.test.ts, policy.test.ts and contact-habitat.test.ts covering all four surfaces.
method: Read-only inspection of the diff and the surrounding decide/compose flow (decision.ts classify path, runtime.ts:103 threshold enforcement, habitat-agent.ts rules/context assembly and the 0.85 clamps, habitat-program.ts manifest prompt interpolation, contact-habitat.ts plan seeding, routed-agent.ts CLASSIFIER_INSTRUCTIONS usage), plus a repo-wide search for other silent/confidence decision surfaces. Verification of the three bundled-source receipt digests was performed by the integrating agent (shasum -a 256) since the reviewer has no shell; the admission validator re-derives every digest fail-closed at build and check time.
result: Ship. Enforcement is code, not prose: runtime.ts:103 ignores respond=true below 0.85, habitat-agent.ts forces respond=false and strips actions/tool under threshold, compose throws NoReplyNeeded, classify runs with allowedTools=[], and the 0.85 gate cannot be reached by a bare share under the new wording. The new rules live in non-evolvable host instruction text, so self-evolution cannot promote them away; plan.guidance remains untrusted style data under host authority. Output schema, reason enum, identity/disclosure/commitment sentences, keyword bypass and all decideReply gates are unchanged. Every one of the four surfaces now carries a regression pin that fails on revert.

findings.finding: The initial regression test pinned only the respond-phase instruction; a revert of the rules contract, CLASSIFIER_INSTRUCTIONS or default plan guidance would have passed the suite.
findings.resolution: Fixed: added a driver-body pin for the rules contract, a CLASSIFIER_INSTRUCTIONS pin in policy.test.ts and a DEFAULT_HABITAT_PLAN.guidance pin in contact-habitat.test.ts.

findings.finding: The instructions said "confidence above 0.85" while the code admits at >= 0.85.
findings.resolution: Fixed: "confidence at or above 0.85 requires an explicit request".

findings.finding: Surfaces diverge slightly on shares combined with a direct address: the rules string silences a share without an explicit question or request while the program instruction permits reply on a direct address alone. Silence-favoring and safe; a share captioned with a request still qualifies as a request under both.
findings.recommendation: Accept; tightening further would narrow the intentionally allowed direct-address case.
